title: Head of Product Marketing
description: Description Ocean is building the future of email security. The attacks getting through today often look completely normal. AI did not invent targeted phishing or social engineering. It changed the economics of it. What once required a highly skilled attacker can now be created at scale, in minutes, and often looks like a completely legitimate message from someone you trust. Ocean is the first agentic email security platform built for this new reality. Our agents investigate suspicious emails the way a great security analyst would: understanding context, following the evidence, and explaining what they find. Founded in 2024 by Shay Shwartz and Oran Moyal, who spent years building targeted email attacks for homeland security, Ocean is the system they know would have stopped them. Today, we protect hundreds of thousands of mailboxes and analyze more than a billion emails every month for companies including Kayak, Headspace, and Fortune 500 enterprises. We're backed by $28M from Lightspeed Venture Partners, Picture Capital, Cerca Partners, and some of the best operators in cybersecurity. We're headquartered in New York and Tel Aviv. And we're just getting started. This is an enormous market opportunity. The problem is getting harder, the category is changing quickly, and Ocean is growing fast. We're hiring our Head of Product Marketing ﻿ This is not a role where you inherit a team or a playbook and spend your time managing it. You'll be the team (at least to start) and define how Ocean tells its story, creates demand, and shows up in the market from the ground up. ﻿ We also don't want you to spend the first month executing a template. We want you to spend it figuring out what Ocean actually needs, in what order, and then tell us. Some of what we think we need will turn out to be wrong, and we'd rather hear that from you early than politely later. You'll work in genuine co-ownership with our head of product, not adjacent to her. Our product and R&D team is in Tel Aviv and ships fast. Our sales and field teams are in the US. You'll be the connective tissue between them, which in practice means holding your early mornings ET open for Israel. It's also the best part of the job, because you'll get closer to how the product actually works than most product marketers ever get to be. You'll help turn a genuinely differentiated product and an incredibly interesting problem into stories and experiences that make people understand Ocean, remember Ocean, and want to learn more. We move quickly. Good ideas can become real very fast. We care about quality, but we don't believe great work requires endless meetings, layers of approval, or bureaucracy. You'll have real ownership, direct access to the people making decisions, and a huge amount of room to make your mark. description: Category: Education Location: The short version What this role is about: Delivering aptitude training that actually prepares students to clear quantitative and problem solving screening rounds at companies and not just teaching formulas for the sake of it. Who we're looking for: Someone who understands that aptitude tests are pattern-recognition problems, not math problems. We're looking for someone who can review a student's mock test and exactly tell us what is going wrong. Why you should apply: You'll become part of a small group of practitioners who don't just teach, they obsess over students' learning, redesign the approach, and measure whether it worked. If you enjoy building from first principles and seeing outcomes improve, you'll find this role deeply rewarding. About us: Kraftshala is India’s largest higher-education institution in terms of marketing placements, with a 94% placement rate. Our programs serve as a talent pipeline for agencies such as Publicis, Dentsu, IPG, and Hiveminds, as well as brands like Nestlé, Nykaa, Google, Lenskart, Zomato, and 500+ other companies. We are backed by eminent investors including ex-unicorn startup founders and CXOs of companies like RedBus, NoBroker, Nestlé, and Performics. The detailed version Aptitude is one of the most common filters students face in placements at top agencies, and analytics companies. Yet most aptitude training follows the same pattern: topic-by-topic formula delivery, practice from standard books, one mock test. Students who already have math confidence do fine. Students who don't, which is most of our cohort leave knowing a formula they'll forget under pressure. At Kraftshala, we believe aptitude should be taught the way companies actually test it: timed, with deliberate traps, and with a clear framework for which questions to attempt first, which to skip, and which to guess on. We're looking for someone who can help us continuously improve this and ensure students are genuinely ready on the day of the test. What you'll spend your time on: Training & Instruction- Conduct live learning sessions across beginner and advanced Aptitude topics while helping students build confidence in solving quantitative problems using mental maths. Diagnosing Student Gaps- Review student performance and identify whether errors come from concept gaps, calculation speed, question misreading, or test anxiety. Design targeted interventions, not a repeat of the original session, but a precise fix for the specific problem. Improving Learning Experiences- Continuously refine curriculum, projects, assessments, and classroom experiences based on student outcomes, hiring partner feedback, and evolving industry expectations. Mentoring Students- Guide students through doubt-solving sessions, assessments, and interview preparation while helping them develop structured quantitative and analytical thinking. Immediate Intervention: Prompt assistance during moments of acute distress or emotional upheaval. Safety and Stabilization: Ensuring the well-being and stability of participants during critical situations. Continuity of Care: Ensuring support during acute moments whilst in treatment ensuring continuity from the group experience to the individual/family experience. Preventing Relapses and Hospitalizations: Reducing the risk of relapses and the need for hospitalizations. Suicide and Self-Harm Prevention: Identifying warning signs and intervening to prevent self-harm or suicide. What does a Crisis Intervention Specialist do? A part-time Crisis Intervention Specialist at Charlie Health plays a crucial role in ensuring the safety and stability of our clients during acute mental health crises. They are responsible for immediate screening and intervention when clients exhibit severe emotional distress or harmful behaviors. Crisis Intervention Specialists collaborate with the clinical team to screen risk of highly acute clients, develop crisis intervention plans, de-escalate dysregulated clients, and connect patients with appropriate resources to facilitate their recovery and well-being within the IOP setting. Pulmovant ’s first investigational candidate, mosliciguat, is designed to provide a novel, once-daily, inhaled treatment option for patients with pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD). A Our sharpest focus is the digital-only segment: thousands of companies with no proactive account coverage. Some have technical resources available to them, but that support is entirely reactive. description: About Nexun Backed by Marguerite, a leading pan-European infrastructure fund, Nexun is a fast-growing renewable project development platform active in Spain, France, Germany, Italy, Poland, and Austria. At Nexun, we are passionate advocates for renewable energy as well as grid infrastructure and are committed to accelerating the transition to a low-carbon economy. Join our diverse team to contribute to projects that positively impact communities across Europe. The Power/Flexibility Markets Analyst leads the commercial development, negotiation, and optimization of Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) projects, including both standalone storage assets and co-located solar-plus-storage projects. The role focuses on identifying best value and route-to-market for our projects, forecasting revenue schemes and offtake contracts possibilities (Tolling Agreements, PPAs), optimizing the commercial design of our plants to derisk projects and maximize their value at the point of sale (RTB) based on a solid market and technical understanding of electricity markets and asset configurations, negotiating PPAs and Tolling agreements. Target countries: Italy, Poland, France as priority and Spain, Austria and Germany as secondary markets Tasks Develop and maintain in-depth knowledge of the electricity markets in at least one of the target countries, including Day-Ahead, Intraday, Ancillary Services, Balancing Markets, Capacity Markets. Monitor regulatory and market developments and evaluate their impact on the revenues and commercial viability of BESS and solar projects. Collect, analyze, and develop electricity price forecasts and revenue projections for standalone BESS and hybrid solar-plus-storage projects. Analyze and compare current route-to-market and optimization models and select and negotiate the optimal role (merchant, tolling, PPA, floor/hybrid structures) for standalone BESS, co-located BESS with photovoltaic (PV) plants, and hybrid renewable energy projects to maximize the RTB value and derisk the projects. Originate, negotiate, and close Tolling Agreements and Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) with offtakers, utilities, traders, on all type of assets (BESS; collocated etc.) Support the preparation of business cases, investment decisions, financial models, and technical/commercial due diligence processes. Build and maintain relationships with key stakeholders across the BESS ecosystem and the different target countries, including utilities, energy traders, optimizers, aggregators, transmission and distribution system operators, regulatory authorities, investors, and asset operators.
